name: Christa Kinsley
subject: Mario for Congress: Moving forward
body:
Dear Friends of Mario,

It's hard to believe it has been a week since the Primary Election, which has given some needed time to process the results. It certainly was not the outcome we had hoped for, and admittedly the results were both sad and surprising to many of us. The strength of our campaign was much stronger than in 2022 and our base of support more active and comprehensive throughout the entire district. We were having daily conversations with voters, and we would comment that it was hard to find a Tenney supporter. People in our district overwhelmingly wanted the same thing - conservative representation based on traditional Republican principles and conviction to stand for America First policies without selling out.

Unfortunately, what we learned is that lies and smears were ultimately more effective. Too many people didn't do the simple job of fact-checking the repeatedly debunked accusations and fear tactics. And in the end, Tenney won the same way she did last time - by deceiving the voters.

On one hand, it makes the 'what do we do next' question challenging. And yet the more time I have and the more I reflect, the answer is simple - we do what we have always done. We continue to stand for the truth and principles that made our nation great in every place we find ourselves. This race gave us the opportunity to do that on a Congressional level throughout our district. But we have these opportunities daily, whether great or small.

One of my favorite Founding Father quotes is from John Quincy Adams who said, "Duty is ours. Results are God's." It is our job to speak and live the truth, to stand for and uphold righteous values - in our own lives, in our communities, in our nation. God will use that for His purpose and in His time.

So what next? Get to know your neighbors. Talk about the issues impacting our communities. Take action where you can. Know your history. Know your Constitution. Be courageous. Though our society is gaslighting these things now, a time will come when others are ready to have open eyes and see the truth. We need to be ready and able to lead and point them back to what is true.

As far as the campaign... a final thing we need your help with -

SIGNS - Our campaign signs will need to be taken down, specifically in public areas. If you see our signs on a roadside or street corner, please pull them. Feel free to hang on to the signs or, if you have a collection and want to return them to Mario, they can be dropped off at Geneva Granite in Geneva.

We don't know what the future holds - either the future of the campaign or future of the nation. But let's be resolved to continue to live out our citizenship the way our nation was designed and always stand for the principles of liberty.

It has been a tremendous blessing for me to be able to support a candidate who spoke the truth and refused to cede the moral high ground, even in the face of baseless slander. I am so grateful to Mario for making the sacrifice of running and giving us all the opportunity to support someone with true courage of conviction and integrity. It was one of the best votes I have had the privilege to cast.

It has also been a blessing and encouragement working with each one of you. While on a personal level, the results of this race were discouraging, it is knowing each of you and seeing your conviction in action that gives me hope that all is not lost. The small minority 'keen to set brushfires of freedom in the minds of men' is still there, and I have been honored to stand with you all in that cause. May God give us wisdom and courage as we move forward together in the great cause of liberty.

Have a wonderful summer and God bless each of you.

For Liberty,
Christa Kinsley
Field Director

I'm going head-to-head with Adam Schiff in November. Democrat policies have brought America to its knees. There's fear of walking down the street because of rampant crime, homelessness, and drug addiction. The cost of living is exploding and for the first time causing more people to leave California. Joe Biden, Adam Schiff and the rest of the Democrats don't care one bit that Americans are having a hard time. I'd go even further to say they welcome the misery so they can keep folks down and dependent. And that's why I'm running for Senate. **_We Republicans_ pulled our country out of the 1970's Democratic malaise by electing Ronald Reagan.** And I believe we can do it again by putting classic conservative values at the heart of everything we do. But there is no way I can pull it off without you. **[**Will you rush a contribution to my campaign of $35 or more today?**](http://links.gopmembership.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=f740177833dd44cea55c7d42e693cc2b&_e=3hHdxGY5IwqR7ueLUUdVOJyzZre7d0KlnU7ZIiBsDlmiCAW2GBNqgncnN0Xkr6EXwS1ZK6aW7JumZe7pARoRnBCU7TvQcX1Es_s8oKQRiJ39gfJlqB5sg2llXgEkVC_qeqmuolebE6a1gK8jxS-aYQRbEo6OdYtD9dDLKuyLvDufy-u3FmppjQr3Rz2QxYT4pjZ_waUC7Z0LilMGPT3sMNBBIVB2hELkj1hNWY49XKgD6_pWe8h62dQUzLtIUbk5bSRdj8md3bZy1MV4oGwDCI35YdihEAJbU8ZA-wS0XBK4vuifgGXaC4KLO4Hkx4lwwK498XQR65u62caoPkRmH9ZqkUBEsVywUxIASn9sXSlC9u3MeWhfEdE_P1gPwUoKhv9Lcfy4qWZPtl2efQMB0w%3D%3D)** I've lived and worked in California for over 50 years, and I can tell you -\- voters here have had it with the Democrats like I've never seen before. They are hungry for change, and if you and I work together to reach voters in every neighborhood, on every beach, in every corner of California... I know we can turn this historic opportunity into a _**Republican win**_. I'm fighting for the soul of the state I love -- but make no mistake -- I'm not just taking the field for Californians. When we win here... when we rip this seat out the hands of the radical Adam Schiff... **...we start the nationwide Republican Comeback Rally our country desperately needs.** Thank you and God Bless,

subject: Young people aren't the problem for Democrats. Young men are.
body:
Democrats are right to worry about losing young voters to Trump, to third parties, or to apathy. But the media narrative is too broad in its focus.

| |
---|---|---
| | | Forwarded this email? [Subscribe here](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.I6aUkYLvrrFBT7QfeJWHvAMXSBrxajRcHft2ZdBs2rg?) for more
---
Politics is full of universal truths, axioms, and unquestioned orthodoxy. We're here to take a closer look at some of that.
Welcome to **Not Quite Right ...** Where we break down where unchallenged assumptions are wrong.
* * *
# [Young people aren't the problem for Democrats. Young men are.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=145882496&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ1ODgyNDk2LCJpYXQiOjE3MTk4NTI0OTYsImV4cCI6MTcyMjQ0NDQ5NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.AwrXt9uuIz7FzPg_mr9P9hZBLl5cpdpXShvJryVIvWs)
### Democrats are right to worry about losing young voters to Trump, to third parties, or to apathy. But the media narrative is too broad in its focus.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Jul 1
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvYmVuc2FtdWVscy9wL3lvdW5nLXBlb3BsZS1hcmVudC10aGUtcHJvYmxlbS1mb3I_.L2BWKQ-AQyC5wiL4eheSVm27Nvs3SntA41H4i6NXrP0?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/young-people-arent-the-problem-for?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store)
---
If you've been following politics at all for the last couple of months, there's a consistent theme that you've probably seen: young voters are leaving the Democratic Party, or at the very least are leaving Biden.
It's been reported [time](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/edcb0582-0893-4146-aee0-ff2a1da7b5ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [time](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6e86510e-a017-494c-97c9-555929ee7d83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [time](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/39bc9603-0a6a-4be4-a0c5-7345398c04b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [time](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4fbb70c3-922d-4746-8a52-a79caf918ab0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) again. It's been reported in [left-leaning](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6d2cbeab-9869-4002-a656-bae5e697451d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [right-leaning outlets](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e5e153a0-66b5-4afe-a403-204edea5616e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It's inescapable. If you want to see Trump lose, it doesn't paint a good picture.
And as someone who _really_ wants Trump to lose, here's what's **Not Quite Right ...** It's not that all young voters are moving away from Democrats. The shift that we're seeing is almost entirely attributable to young men.
### The chasm between young men and young women
This [recent poll of 18-to-29-year-olds nationwide](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a1e12051-4b64-4f1b-ac0c-23abb0aec241?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is jarring:
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a1e12051-4b64-4f1b-ac0c-23abb0aec241?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For a while now, there has been a [gap in how men and women vote](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/16dea91a-1ce9-447e-8728-b20039a12124?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Yes, [that's accelerated](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9793444d-8781-4ea8-a215-cb3a2ab4f8f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but the phenomenon is nothing new.
What appears to be new is the growing gap between _young_ men and women--[even as of the last election cycle](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9a07eab9-5c38-47ca-9d29-71f498ea6a61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), that wasn't really happening. Now all of a sudden, it's something we're [pretty](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d6dfcfa2-0b8e-4e45-baee-f6ed59ee3ae8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [consistently](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/00811b1c-fb6f-46d6-83e9-61b0c6c6a899?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [seeing](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/98d320eb-d579-4240-90fd-0fa40cfe7d43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in polling.
This isn't unique to the United States, by the way. We're seeing [similar swings in other countries](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ce94cf45-1edf-4b1b-84a6-951ee779a204?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) around the world too. So while some of this is probably attributable to Trump, certainly not all of it is.
### What's going on?
Generally, I don't think Democrats do a particularly good job talking about just how hard it is to be a young man today, and I think it's worth outlining the extent of some of those challenges:
1. In the United States, men are [nearly 4x more likely than women](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/98ed4540-93bf-4583-a629-9b767a494eec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to die by suicide. Among younger men, [that imbalance is even more extreme](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8ab2bfe2-7a14-4599-9b60-166835d219f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).1
2. The opioid crisis is an enormous problem for everyone in America. But [men are 2-3x more likely to die of opioid overdoses than women](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b9e863bc-0f53-4ac6-ba65-fcede2fc3d78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [younger people are more likely than older people to die of an overdose](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/14d9b836-7f3b-4bd4-96b4-13c45013fccd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Young men are hit by both.
3. Young men have [higher unemployment rates](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/61708bd9-cf95-4652-9c27-19902d96f5c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than young women and than the rest of the population. And if that weren't enough, some of the jobs most commonly held by men are at the highest risk of disruption by AI and technology. Trucking, [the most common job for men in the U.S.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/5a4baeae-5933-4797-a667-a246b7bb53d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is at the doorstep of a [self-driving revolution](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1b9eed16-42a7-4ae3-ae45-b78824d630f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that will lead to a dramatic change in the workforce.2
4. Very much related, young men are [attaining college degrees at a significantly lower rate than women](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/dd192962-adbb-49cb-914b-26c0168e9b23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): among people ages 25-34, 46% of women but only 36% of men have a bachelor's degree. Women have been graduating college at a higher rate than men for a while now, but those differences have been accelerating in the last decade or so:
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d2104dde-97ce-4ffc-bde3-22833cc4ee86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
5. The [crisis of loneliness](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6117da6f-a1b4-4bbe-8f8e-655d598a45ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)3 in America is an enormous problem and impacts everyone. But the problem is [more acute among young people ](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/369ddae3-18a8-4045-8776-9194f956548a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[and](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/369ddae3-18a8-4045-8776-9194f956548a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ more acute among men](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/369ddae3-18a8-4045-8776-9194f956548a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),4 so it's particularly brutal for young men.
6. Very much related, from _[The Hill](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/430c86d5-ce89-4824-a928-9369177894f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ : "More than 60 percent of young men are single, nearly twice the rate of unattached young women, signaling a larger breakdown in the social, romantic and sexual life of the American male."5

In short: a lot of the incredible social challenges that many Americans are confronting today--addiction and loneliness and a feeling of insecurity in one's job and a bunch of other things--seem to be hitting young men particularly hard.
[Start Survey](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/98a45536-67d0-474a-a717-6ec690c3e68d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### Why is all of this making young men more Republican?
Some of what's driving the gender divide among young voters isn't just that men are moving away from Democrats but also that [young women are becoming more liberal](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8229f4a3-27e4-4c03-8826-32ff7c443235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And some of it is demographic; [people without college degrees are more likely to vote Republican](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/544705f2-e6a6-4240-8e08-1c76b8b7ce76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and as established above, far more young women than young men have college degrees.
I've also read other explanations--a [backlash from #MeToo](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d1cfcbae-5ddf-4e2e-aa45-ab48cb749ade?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or from [cancel culture](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/29f52725-1e05-415c-adfd-974db8f11b66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for example--that may or may not be true in part, but I think the truth is simpler than that.
More than young women, **many young men feel like the status quo isn 't working for them.** Today, Democrats represent the status quo, and Republicans represent what feels like--to them--a needed change.
Obviously, I don't agree with that. I don't think these issues are attributable to Biden or to Democrats. In fact, **I believe that[a lot of what Biden has accomplished really helps young men](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4f59a5f4-3be0-4216-ac0a-a9f4c4239007?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
But I don't hear many Democrats talking directly to young men. And say what you will about Trump, **he is probably better at courting young men than Biden is** , and he's doing it more explicitly.
Remember that the youngest voters in the '24 election were only nine years old when Trump announced he was running for President in 2015. For the youngest voters, their whole conscious lives have been spent in the Trump era. Much of what we see as aberrational is, for younger voters, their normal.
The argument that Trump is a norm-busting candidate, therefore, doesn't resonate with younger voters. If you see both parties as corrupt and rigged, as [most Americans do](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/39030292-f099-481a-9347-f76def72a4d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), you might as well vote for the candidate who shakes up the status quo.
I think two other key things are at play here as well. First, the Democrats--rightly--expend a lot of energy attacking extremist positions the Republican Party is taking on abortion access.
It's a critical wedge issue, but it's also one that matters much more to young women than young men. "Women's reproductive health" is the [fourth-most important issue for female voters under 30](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a1e12051-4b64-4f1b-ac0c-23abb0aec241?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). For young men, it's not even in the top 10.
### Growing extremism
Second, there is an alarming thread of extremism in young men that's absolutely driving part of what we're seeing. Young men are, on the whole, still [more liberal than older men](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6fc7de55-992d-4dc6-b622-035781e0f58a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but **the most extreme young men are more extreme than the most extreme older men**.
[Young men repudiate feminism more than older men](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/63fe6334-9cca-46ed-8cb1-7115736d915b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for example. They're far more likely to say that the [use of violence in politics is justifiable](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a7ea4c10-c713-45c2-bb66-c0445eb70cac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Needless to say, this is horrifying.6 And again, this extremism is hardly limited to the United States--in fact, the problem appears to be more pronounced in other parts of the world:
* The United Kingdom is having an [election later this week](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/22ddccb3-e450-4d91-8a7f-0cc22898a23b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and polling I've seen for that has anywhere from [1%](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7fa30ba0-b66f-47d2-9469-217cb08bb8af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [13%](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8fbc57b2-7dbb-4d7a-9abb-717681e8e97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of younger voters supporting the incumbent Conservative Party. It seems very likely that more men under 35 are going to vote for the extremist Reform Party--a party whose candidates [keep praising Hitler](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/554d8ee2-0127-4ac3-9800-fff5cd396a1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [doing all sorts of other racist nonsense](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/33e8290e-5782-4a98-b1a5-6e5400884b7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--than the Conservatives.7 Even [more startling data in the UK](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/028866df-9340-494f-9d06-f2a53a356f29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "Almost half of young men (46%) believe that political violence can be necessary in extreme circumstances."
* From _[The Economist](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/67a40375-e37e-47e6-9288-358264e6e148?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ : "Nearly 80% of South Korean men in their 20s say that men are discriminated against. Barely 30% of men over 60 agree, making their views indistinguishable from those of women in their 20s or 60s."

### Democrats, acknowledge the challenges of young men
Nothing here is to dismiss the very real concerns that young women are facing in this country: they [still make less money than men](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8727abe4-0445-4c12-b326-b263faa88e24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),8 they're [way less represented in political office](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1b1bdbbd-956e-4ac6-97d0-c5ad5704d80a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [access to good health care is being stripped](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c5587130-6b86-4891-8a2d-7efb1436acfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from them because of extremist Republican policies, etc.
But: I hear Democrats talking about all of this more. What I don't hear are very many Democrats trying to talk to young men. Republicans are doing just that, and their messages--especially from online influencers--are in many cases outright toxic.
**Democrats need to do more to reach out to young men.** Recognize what they're experiencing and what they're feeling.
Men have all kinds of systemic societal advantages--I'm not arguing that point at all. But I worry that maybe that's kept Democrats from doing more to acknowledge just how hard it is to be a young man right now.
Recognizing their genuine challenges doesn't validate the extremism or "men's rights" or anything of the sort. If anything, it begins to diffuse it.
[Start Survey](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/98a45536-67d0-474a-a717-6ec690c3e68d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Finally, please take a moment to fill out this survey. I'd love your thoughts and ideas.
1
It is worth noting that the ratio at which men _attempt_ suicide vs. women is not as extreme, and that difference has to do with the fact that men are far more likely than women to [attempt suicides using guns](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b2575fc7-1d02-449d-ac2e-3f2acb67e263?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Guns are tragically effective as a method of suicide, and in 2021, [54% of all firearm deaths in the U.S. were suicides](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3939b23a-677d-424b-b595-facbd61d56e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). According to [Mike Anestis](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/276d8132-9008-4ea1-901e-c90cc0960381?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a professor at the Rutgers School of Public Health: "Only 2% to 3% of the folks who attempt suicide using an overdose die. Almost 95% of folks who use a firearm do."
This is part of the reason why laws like [Donna's Law](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ae37cd2b-9f7c-4b84-a943-ce86543ae34d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which allows people struggling with mental health to put themselves on a do-not-buy list for firearms, are so important. It saves lives. Donna's Law is on the books in Utah, Virginia, and Washington state so far.
2
On the other hand, the most common jobs for women are [nurses and teachers](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4a1a4549-cf1d-47e2-8faf-2f35130529cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), occupations that aren't likely to be hit by automation or AI particularly soon.
3
Both _[The Washington Post](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c8e0e03b-20da-44b0-b088-8b558a9e5c5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ and _[The New York Times](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a7eaf034-5d35-4022-9e4f-4fda7a053d7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ have written articles recently about how to make friends. The fact that we need those articles written is maybe not a great sign for society.
4
This data, [reported by ](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9f5b362e-e6f3-46b5-9933-af6e430e6771?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[The Economist](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9f5b362e-e6f3-46b5-9933-af6e430e6771?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ (and I'm sure others), is really striking: "In 1990, 55% of American men reported having at least six close friends; today only 27% do. The survey found that 15% of men have no close friendships at all, a fivefold increase since 1990."
5
There's a lot to unpack here, but the dating market--one that generally impacts young people much more than older people--has [some extreme inefficiencies](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6921864c-6ace-4e0b-8718-1c1cff97418a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), if you want to call them that: "Sixty-one percent of single men were looking for a relationship or dates, but only 38 percent of women reported doing so."
As _[The Economist](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1b75412a-b880-43c7-8d38-a6746c84d523?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ noted](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1b75412a-b880-43c7-8d38-a6746c84d523?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (in the context of nations that practice polygamy, but the point is worth thinking about), "when large numbers of men are doomed to bachelorhood, they get desperate" and violence often follows.
This is all _way_ outside what I'm talking about here, but it unfortunately, at least to a degree, ties into the extremism among pockets of younger men that I wrote about above.
6
This is a vast topic that I won't get into here, but there are a bunch of reasons for this: a breakdown in communities, [extremism on the internet](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/86fd0337-e871-4ec0-8b48-2bea0d10481f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the "[manosphere](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/40793f5a-c01a-410a-af29-4c02001d4755?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," the popularity of people like [Andrew Tate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/412b0023-ef76-4e2a-aa44-bf647c7e730e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and Jordan Peterson and others on YouTube and social media, etc.
7
It's an imperfect parallel, but this would be akin to a bunch of young American men deciding to forego the Republicans and vote for the [Constitution Party](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/389a172d-b78c-411a-ba26-f59032babb5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or someone equally nutty and right-wing.
8
Though that gap is closing among younger Americans.

body:
Judicial Watch announced recently that it received eight pages of records from the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) showing Mike Morell, former acting CIA director under President Obama, requesting CIA permission to publish a letter by former intelligence community leaders stating that they believed the laptop emails exposing Hunter Biden’s connections to Ukraine were Russian disinformation.

| **IMPORTANT PRESS RELEASE**
---
| | | **Kern Campaign Releases New Ad to Combat “Dangerous” Use of “Fake Electors” Term**
---
| Glendale, AZ – The Kern campaign today released a new campaign ad that thoroughly debunks the term “fake electors” that is often used by the media in connection with a nine-count indictment handed down by Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes in April against State Senator Anthony Kern and 17 other defendants.

---
| **WATCH & SHARE THIS 60-SECOND VIDEO

_“Almost Everybody Loves Anthony Kern”_**
---
[ ](https://votekern.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2add33eab54cf78e2fdebc3c8&id=e7be2cf485&e=b78dc6f299)
| Kern and his team maintain the proper term is **“alternate electors”** and back up their claim with an op-ed written in early 2024 by a Harvard Law Professor. Kern is running for Congress in CD-8 and early voting for the primary election starts in just one week, making the false claims against Kern even more damaging to his campaign.

In the indictment, Mayes alleges that Kern and the other defendants engaged in a _“scheme to prevent the lawful transfer of the presidency”_ by falsely presenting a document that alleged that 11 of the defendants were the proper Trump-aligned electors despite an initial state-level determination by then-Gov. Ducey that the Biden-aligned electors were the proper Arizona electors.

Kern and his team believe that the **“alternate”** slate of electors was necessary and lawful to preserve the alternate slate while the legal and federal constitutional process played out after the election up to and including congressional review on January 6, 2021, pursuant to the Electoral Count Act of 1887.

Had any of the lawsuits - or the congressional review - challenging the validity of the election been successful and led to Trump receiving a higher vote total in Arizona than Biden, the **“alternate”** slate of electors would have been employed. Without the backup slate in place, Trump could not have been named president even if he had prevailed in any venue, according to the Kern campaign team.

The Kern team asserts that the term _“fake elector”_ demonstrates _“actual malice”_ towards Senator Kern and is only being used to discredit the veteran legislator and to make it falsely appear as if Kern intentionally and willfully tried to deceive the public when in fact, the actions Kern took in December of 2020 were necessary and prudent when considerable doubt and legal challenges existed as to the validity of Joe Biden’s election.

Supporting its claim, the campaign cites Harvard Law Professor Lawrence Lessig, who wrote in the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel in early 2024 and said,

_“There’s an increasingly familiar — and dangerous — way in which the press and public are referring to the presidential electors who, in 2020, gathered to cast their ballots even though the election had not been called for their candidate, Donald Trump.

These electors are called “fake electors...But where there is a good faith question about who the winner in a particular state is, state law should have no power to restrict whether or how presidential electors gather and vote. Their power is federal. They are performing a federal function. State law cannot control that federal function.” _

**The full op-ed piece from Professor Lessig is available[HERE](https://votekern.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2add33eab54cf78e2fdebc3c8&id=1538f4be3b&e=b78dc6f299).**

---
| | **Kern Said He Would Do It Again...**
---
| | [ ](https://votekern.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2add33eab54cf78e2fdebc3c8&id=bb77d82966&e=b78dc6f299)
---

Kern, who was endorsed by President Trump during his state senate campaign in 2022, said he was honored to serve the president as an alternate elector and that he has no regrets about fulfilling the role for the president.

**_“I was honored to be an elector for President Trump in the event we were needed after all the legal dust settled.”_**
---
| Kern said. _**“There was nothing ‘fake’ about what we did, and I would do it again should the need arise. Kris Mayes has no authority to say who the official electors of Arizona are. According to our constitution, only congress has that authority, which they exercised by law on January 6, 2021”.**_

| From the Desk of Dr. Ben Carson: Dear Fellow Patriot,

My name is Dr. Ben Carson, and along with my wife, Candy, I have spent years contemplating the challenges facing American families today.

Our new book, _The Perilous Fight_ , addresses these issues head-on, offering practical insights and solutions to restore and strengthen the family unit.

Why is this important? Because the family's pivotal role in our society is under threat, and without addressing these challenges, our foundational values may be lost. [](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z9tae77q0h557etsmdhoql55sgbn1rc8q6gh9k8g_rp22sh2s8i6ep34s3hmeor4chh2bs) In _The Perilous Fight_ , we dive deep into the social and economic pressures that families face, dissect the erosion of traditional values, and present actionable steps for rebuilding familial bonds. This book isn't just a series of observations; it's a roadmap to a healthier, more stable society through strong family units.

**[**As someone committed to the promotion of truth and values, I am offering you access to the first chapter of our book for free. This limited-time offer will give you a glimpse into the vital issues we explore and the solutions we propose.**](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zci8nie8quphgkt3ffk2q0scip3ungtteq5qshbo_rp22sh2s8i6ep34s3hmeor4chh2bs)** I invite you to request access to your free chapter today if you want to:
* Understand the current challenges American families face;

* Discover actionable steps to strengthen your family and community; and

* Be part of a broader effort to uphold traditional values and promote societal stability

The American Cornerstone Institute is devoted to advancing faith, liberty, community, and life. By downloading the first chapter, you are taking a crucial step towards healing our nation, starting at its very heart--the family.

Don't wait - this free offer is only available for a limited time.

[Click here to download your free chapter of _The Perilous Fight_ now and join us in the mission to strengthen American families.](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zf6k32noe2jrlo65ljfajq3vre52e1q1lqhtj73g_rp22sh2s8i6ep34s3hmeor4chh2bs)

Sincerely,

Dr. Ben Carson

name: Hillsdale College via Restore Our Nation
subject: Before they're gone
body:
Only a fraction of the 16 million Americans who fought bravely in World War II remain with us.

This sponsored message from Restore Our Nation is on behalf of Hillsdale College
[](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/3FoluRCOl25R_O6bEBnreg~~/AARclAA~~~) Dear Fellow American,
Only a fraction of the 16 million Americans who fought bravely in World War II remain with us. This fact means that we’re losing more and more living memory of the greatest armed conflict in human history, which makes the study of World War II even more important.
To this end, Hillsdale College has produced an online course called **“The Second World Wars.”**
**Taught by historian Victor Davis Hanson** , this course explores how the conflict’s diverse theaters, belligerents, and ways of fighting came eventually to define a single war. And it examines the key investments, strategies, and leaders that led the Allied powers to victory over the Axis. [](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/3FoluRCOl25R_O6bEBnreg~~/AARclAA~~~) If you’d like to secure a DVD set before they’re all gone, you can get one shipped directly to your home for any gift of $100 or more to Hillsdale College.
Here’s a secure link to reserve your copy of **“The Second World Wars”** on DVD:
**[https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/support-the-second-world-wars](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/3FoluRCOl25R_O6bEBnreg~~/AARclAA~~~)**
Thank you for preserving liberty for future generations of Americans through education with Hillsdale College!
Best regards,
Jeremiah Regan, Ph.D. Executive Director of Online Learning Hillsdale College
P.S. The **“The Second World Wars”** DVD set is great as a homeschool curriculum or for independent study. Plus, it makes a perfect gift for anyone who wants to know more about the Second World War. **[Reserve your copy now.](https://post.spmailtechnol.com/f/a/3FoluRCOl25R_O6bEBnreg~~/AARclAA~~~)**
---

Friend, We are only 6 days away from the Republican National Convention and the 2024 Summer Meeting of the RNC.
As a member of the RNC's Youth Advisory Council, I will be wheels up for Milwaukee in just 6 days, where I will spend over half of July attending the Summer Meeting and National Convention.
It is the highest honor of my life to represent my generation, Gen Z on the national level to ensure we keep Gen Z conservative.
As we are only 6 days away from Fiserv, I am reaching out to you one last time to humbly ask for your support.
Your generous support of me in my work to save my generation from the perils of liberalism has been incredible and has been felt. Every penny raised has gone to my work in helping guide the RNC in how to win Gen Z and I am excited to pick up where we left off in just 6 days in Milwaukee, WI!
If you are able and willing to contribute to my mission, you will be automatically entered to win a signed RNC Milwaukee 2024 hat like this one:

Peter -
Hey, I wanted to email (again) this morning to thank you for wading through all the other emails and text messages we sent ahead of last night's FEC fundraising deadline.
They are such a huge part of the way we fund this campaign, so I hope you will view them as a small price to pay to keep Kari Lake out of the Senate.

It's humbling.
So thank you again.
Ruben Gallego

Peter, During CNN’s presidential debate we heard about so many things. We heard about Donald Trump and porn stars. We heard Joe Biden declare that _“we finally beat Medicare”_ whatever that means.

You know what we didn’t hear about? A plan to solve the hunger crisis in America.

Meanwhile 26% of Americans in a recent Gallup survey shared that there were times last year when they didn’t have enough money to buy food for themselves or their family.

[ ](https://www.jillstein2024.com/donate?e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=1_in_4_americans&n=2)

**1 in 4 Americans.** This is why we needed every ballot-qualified candidate to be on that debate stage. Instead of arguing about golf, we should've seen every candidate discussing how they would keep those who live in the richest nation in the world _**fed**_.

As painful as the duopoly debate debacle was to watch, it was a great reminder as to why we must keep fighting to get Jill Stein elected. She is the only candidate with a path to the White House who supports an economic bill of rights.

That means electing a president who believes everyone has the right to a living-wage job, guaranteed livable income, housing, healthcare, childcare, lifelong education, secure retirement, utilities, healthy food and clean water. That’s how we end hunger in America. _**Peter, if you agree with Jill that now is the time to demand an economic bill of rights, will you contribute $25 or any amount you can right now?**_

body:
We have an inspiring group of energetic, diverse leaders heading to Chicago to represent our community in the final nomination process.

| Peter,

As you may know, we are just a couple of months away from the Democratic National Convention. As the Democratic Congresswoman for PA-07, I had the honor of helping select the delegates to represent our community at the Convention. Now, I consider it my responsibility to help these delegates get to Chicago.

We have an inspiring group of energetic, diverse leaders heading to Chicago to represent our community in the final nomination process. I trust these leaders to support what is best for our country come August. However, most of the individuals selected as delegates do not have the personal means to fund the journey to Chicago on their own. [_**To support these delegates, the Lehigh County Democratic Party is hosting a fundraising reception tonight at 7pm in Allentown. | _**Survey says: Schools skirt parental consent**_
---
| [ ](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=52a199a8e0&e=b7b3eddce2)

|
* * *
---
|
#### Right to Know requests reveal that some school districts failed to comply with policies and federal laws regarding student surveys.
---
|
#### By Beth Ann Rosica
---
| "As a parent of a second grader, would you be ok if your child was asked at school to rate this statement as true or false?

'Someone you know, even a relative, might want to touch your private parts in a way that feels confusing.'

Without context, this is a concerning question. Even with context, for some parents, the statement may be disturbing.
....
There is a delicate balance between ensuring that abused children get the help they need and discussing sensitive topics in school that some parents prefer to have at home..."

body:
The New York Times’ blatant hypocrisy rears its ugly head following last week’s debate

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88063285/482996674/2130526953?refcode=emwrapper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjA4MGQ2MjctZGMzNy1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=0-8V9ZIa1bR1DsjF59pU7wPlRxFm9QYGrM4icgUeunc=&emci=52ad39c0-d837-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=b080d627-dc37-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=14016711)
Peter,
In case you missed it, _The New York Times_ ’ editorial board penned an op-ed on Friday calling for President Biden to step down following his performance in Thursday’s debate:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88063287/482996676/-593472309?refcode=20240701-EM-NYTDebate&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjA4MGQ2MjctZGMzNy1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=0-8V9ZIa1bR1DsjF59pU7wPlRxFm9QYGrM4icgUeunc=)
_The Times_ ’ decision is controversial because, as Barack Obama tweeted in the hours following the debate, “bad debates happen. Trust me, I know.”
By pointing out his own poor debate performance in 2012, Obama cautioned against simply ignoring three and a half years' worth of Biden administration success because of a bad 90-minute debate performance.
But rushing to judgment is precisely what the _Times_ did by calling on Biden to drop out. And the decision is even more puzzling when you consider what the same editorial board wrote in May when Donald Trump was convicted of 34 felonies:
_“The jurors have delivered their verdict, as the voters will in November. If the Republic is to survive, all of us – including Mr. Trump – should abide by both, regardless of the outcome.”_
**Trump’s crimes, of course, are far more severe than a single poor debate performance. In his New York trial, Trump was convicted of a hush-money scheme designed to influence the outcome of the 2016 election. It’s not like Trump’s disregard for the rule of law, and democracy is an isolated incident – this is the same guy who lied about the 2020 election being stolen and used that lie to justify an attempted coup of our government on January 6th. **
**[We’ll discuss more about the _New York Times_ ' hypocrisy and why it matters in a moment, but if you’re ready to support COURIER’s mission to expose bias and provide a factual alternative, can you contribute $20 now?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88063288/482996678/-593472309?refcode=20240701-EM-NYTDebate&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjA4MGQ2MjctZGMzNy1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=0-8V9ZIa1bR1DsjF59pU7wPlRxFm9QYGrM4icgUeunc=)**
Peter, this isn’t the first time this year the _New York Times_ has been questioned for bias against President Biden.
In April, _Politico_ reported a “feud” between the Biden Campaign and the _Times_ , with the campaign frustrated that the _Times_ was:
_“falling short in a make-or-break moment for American democracy, stubbornly refusing to adjust its coverage as it strives for the appearance of impartial neutrality, often blurring the asymmetries between former President Donald Trump and Biden when it comes to their perceived flaws and vastly different commitments to democratic principles.” - Politico, April 24th, 2024._
**Sound familiar?** 🤔
And remember this hero shot that ran on the front page of the _Times_ when Trump entered his not-guilty plea to charges that he endangered national security by flagrantly mishandling classified documents?
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88063289/482996680/-593472309?refcode=20240701-EM-NYTDebate&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjA4MGQ2MjctZGMzNy1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=0-8V9ZIa1bR1DsjF59pU7wPlRxFm9QYGrM4icgUeunc=)
In fact, the _Times_ ' bias has been so alarming that _Salon_ published a piece titled “There is something wrong at the _New York Times_ ,” in which they discussed the seemingly favorable coverage Donald Trump was getting in comparison to the Biden campaign:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88063301/482996682/-593472309?refcode=20240701-EM-NYTDebate&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjA4MGQ2MjctZGMzNy1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=0-8V9ZIa1bR1DsjF59pU7wPlRxFm9QYGrM4icgUeunc=)
So here’s the problem: the _New York Times_ is trusted, widely read, and even called a “paper of record,” meaning that it is recognized that its publications have a profound impact on our democracy.
So it matters when the _Times_ calls for Biden to step down because of his performance on the debate stage. And when they sweep Trump’s crimes under the rug and put it on the voters to decide whether a convicted felon should be our next president, that matters, too.
**So here’s our promise.** We will never draw a false equivalency between Donald Trump and Joe Biden at COURIER. We will also never be afraid to call out the _Times_ or any other legacy media for blatant hypocrisy in their reporting.
And we’re offering a meaningful alternative by making trustworthy journalism freely available in eleven battleground states because we want voters to know the truth in what could be the most critical election of our lifetime.

clean_body: The New York Times’ blatant hypocrisy rears its ugly head following last week’s debate Peter, In case you missed it, The New York Times ’ editorial board penned an op-ed on Friday calling for President Biden to step down following his performance in Thursday’s debate: = The Times ’ decision is controversial because, as Barack Obama tweeted in the hours following the debate, “bad debates happen. Trust me, I know.” By pointing out his own poor debate performance in 2012, Obama cautioned against simply ignoring three and a half years' worth of Biden administration success because of a bad 90-minute debate performance. But rushing to judgment is precisely what the Times did by calling on Biden to drop out. And the decision is even more puzzling when you consider what the same editorial board wrote in May when Donald Trump was convicted of 34 felonies: “The jurors have delivered their verdict, as the voters will in November. If the Republic is to survive, all of us – including Mr. Trump – should abide by both, regardless of the outcome.” Trump’s crimes, of course, are far more severe than a single poor debate performance. In his New York trial, Trump was convicted of a hush-money scheme designed to influence the outcome of the 2016 election. It’s not like Trump’s disregard for the rule of law, and democracy is an isolated incident – this is the same guy who lied about the 2020 election being stolen and used that lie to justify an attempted coup of our government on January 6th. = Peter, this isn’t the first time this year the New York Times has been questioned for bias against President Biden. In April, Politico reported a “feud” between the Biden Campaign and the Times , with the campaign frustrated that the Times was: “falling short in a make-or-break moment for American democracy, stubbornly refusing to adjust its coverage as it strives for the appearance of impartial neutrality, often blurring the asymmetries between former President Donald Trump and Biden when it comes to their perceived flaws and vastly different commitments to democratic principles.” - Politico, April 24th, 2024. Sound familiar? 🤔 And remember this hero shot that ran on the front page of the Times when Trump entered his not-guilty plea to charges that he endangered national security by flagrantly mishandling classified documents? = In fact, the Times ' bias has been so alarming that Salon published a piece titled “There is something wrong at the New York Times ,” in which they discussed the seemingly favorable coverage Donald Trump was getting in comparison to the Biden campaign: = So here’s the problem: the New York Times is trusted, widely read, and even called a “paper of record,” meaning that it is recognized that its publications have a profound impact on our democracy. So it matters when the Times calls for Biden to step down because of his performance on the debate stage. And when they sweep Trump’s crimes under the rug and put it on the voters to decide whether a convicted felon should be our next president, that matters, too. So here’s our promise. We will never draw a false equivalency between Donald Trump and Joe Biden at COURIER. We will also never be afraid to call out the Times or any other legacy media for blatant hypocrisy in their reporting. body:
Thank you so much, Peter.
#
Hi Peter, it’s Lucas Kunce with a quick update about our Q2 fundraising.
**We’re still counting all the numbers, but it’s safe to say that after our big push this weekend we had our best quarter yet.** My team will share more about all that soon, but for now I just wanted to reach out to say thank you.
Insiders thought I was crazy when I decided to run this campaign the right way — without any money from corporate PACs or Big Oil + Big Pharma execs. But real people like you have stepped up to prove them wrong by helping us hit our goals at nearly every single deadline.
That support has allowed us to hold Josh Hawley accountable for crusading against reproductive rights and embarrassing our state. It’s helped us earn major in-state and national endorsements from groups like the Missouri AFL-CIO, Missouri Fire Fighters, VoteVets, and End Citizens United. And it’s made this race our best chance to flip a U.S. Senate seat this November.
We’ve got some serious MO-mentum. **But now, with the first six months of 2024 over, we’ve still got the most important work ahead of us.**
From scaling up our campaign staff to launching TV ads and getting organizers on the ground, we’ve got to make sure our campaign has the resources to keep exposing Hawley’s record and getting our message in front of voters. And your continued support is what makes that possible for our movement.
I can’t tell you how much it means to me that you’re part of this team, Peter. I know that together, we can defeat Josh Hawley, flip Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat, and take back power for working Missourians this November.
Now, let’s keep moving.
— Lucas Kunce

While Washington remains gridlocked, Dr. Raul Ruiz is committed to serving and helping constituents with the problems they have with the federal government and cutting red tape. If you’d like to unsubscribe, click here. # [#]
Hi there,

I’ll never get tired of saying this: thank you! Just last week, my re-election campaign for Congress in CA-25 faced its toughest fundraising challenge yet, and falling short wasn’t an option if we want to ensure our district stays blue this November.

A show of strength was critical, and that’s exactly what we did.

That’s why I’m grateful for you and your support. It’s what carried us to and past our goal — and what’s going to lead us to victory in the fall. This isn’t a fight for one, or even two — this is a mass movement to defend the rights we hold dear.

We know all too well that in this day and age, nothing is guaranteed.

From reproductive healthcare to our ability to live in a clean and safe environment, we’ve watched as MAGA extremists in our government have sought to systematically undermine so much of the progress we’ve made in recent years. And so I’ll say it again: nothing is guaranteed.

But there is one thing that we can be sure of: regardless of how far they go, how many of our liberties they strip away — we’re not going anywhere. Because this is about more than you and me — this is about securing our collective future, and that of California’s 25th.

And it’s through our work — together — that we’ll do just that. If you didn’t get a chance to chip in before the deadline, you can still do so and make just as big of an impact by clicking here. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruiz-em-fr-july24]

Thank you for standing with me,

Raul

In the summer of 1990, Raul walked in the desert heat from business to business in the Coachella Valley asking them to invest in their community by contributing to his education. With each investment for college, he made a promise to come back home and serve his community as a physician. In 2012, he decided to take his service to the community to the next level by running for Congress. Dr. Ruiz needs our help to continue fighting for us in Congress and to flip the House blue this November.

| | | "No."
"Sorry, I'm not interested."
"I can't make a difference."

These are all phrases I've heard too often in my life.

80% of people I reach out to share my story tell me one of those three phrases.

**Friend, I believe in the American Dream.** **I 'm the son of a bartender who grew up to become a United States Senator. I'm proud to say I'm one of the lucky folks living the American Dream!**

_**That 's why I'm writing you today.**_ My story is uniquely American. I could tell you that I did this all on my own. I could tell you that I simply pulled myself up by the bootstraps and one day I was a U.S. Senator. _But that 's just not true; I had **tons** of help._

**I have _always_ relied on support from grassroots conservatives like you, Friend. **When I ran for Florida House in West Miami, I didn't have big corporate donors backing me. And when I ran for Senate against Charlie Crist, there were no megadonors backing me. _**[Everything I've achieved has been because of folks like _you!_](https://links.conservativesgive.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=ee1181effdbc40a79a3c845139163ace&_e=70FvHjy33iQE_b-X7Cj6w7jxyPTDXgH4DkZWxP19UkzWI0rYX6lZK4kLVZFAC8YDvjHONsrXxrJr7EKSyaWPbpADaumsLOAGoGHSZwLp1O2UAUO4XAulMrb9n4GSAu-nTNjLFvjqQq7_jIar7Qye72hDnVhsr35Gkq24hRWaU-gnFPavE4xx9RGDyDXcldR_blkS-9oTKhhIivqmEyfBddxc3EtgD5xYesH6TH3DSUiiuMkVyhMFqMwjmKhtkNIGsmS4Dwjgkwpg22NfbiGHAJw7vD9sirJf7fSxnyefmv3sxaPbGhqbH3LzMuQhQo6QIlUhSafGnQ-4lVlk5iYOkGxvV5QP7mFsUfdLO97IFx9T-i6t_wahKo0eSAoDSrwYGYBcetRgfYf-cgp_Z_iXeo1Uet_0f3lwNr8lm0lvQBitVoFlU8QX5aCqMC8XIUFjkJBJ364r27b__8rcnQ2uyAF3symxseovar5tBCKdn1U%3D "Everything I’ve achieved has been because of folks like you!")**_

As I've written before, the U.S. Supreme Court has--throughout its history--[consistently undermined human rights and human dignity](https://substack.com/redirect/b9381847-1820-42cc-8e76-ce8caa0ddb9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the United States. Now, the Court continues its shameful history with at least six new reckless rulings that ultimately reshape and undermine our democracy for the worse. It is not an overstatement to say this further fast-tracks us towards fascism and dictatorship.
Here's a recap of six of Court's most egregious rulings this session, and how it affects us. **Let 's Address This.**
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2550223&post_id=146173786&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ2MTczNzg2LCJpYXQiOjE3MTk4NjM1MjksImV4cCI6MTcyMjQ1NTUyOSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI1NTAyMjMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.m3Lrm9ffAdcJhOmPFQxakdR5AwBXv_fe1RC6zz9H2KE)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e300b8f8-7d91-4ccd-bdf3-a59a33ccfa85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The justices of the Supreme Court. Credit: Erin Schaff/The New York Times
### 1\. Presidential Immunity Expanded
Raise your hand if you remember learning about the separation of powers, and the fact that we have a democratically elected President with limited powers, not a fascist empowered dictator with unlimited powers? The Supreme Court is here to tell you that you're wrong. The Court has ruled that while the President has no immunity for unofficial acts, a President can claim immunity for allegedly unofficial acts if they can argue these acts were part of their official duties. Justice Sonia Sotomayor accurately lambasted the absurdity of this [ruling](https://substack.com/redirect/48fb701d-2f84-4e4f-ab53-ecd7be0abffc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> "Today's decision to grant former Presidents criminal immunity reshapes the institution of the Presidency. It makes a mockery of the principle, foundational to our Constitution and system of Government, that no man is above the law. The majority today endorses an expansive vision of Presidential immunity that was never recognized by the Founders, any sitting President, the Executive Branch, or even President Trump's lawyers, until now. Settled understandings of the Constitution are of little use to the majority in this case, and so it ignores them.
This ruling additionally delays significant legal cases past critical election dates, laying the groundwork for potential abuse of presidential power and further entrenching autocracy. As long as the President can make some excuse that his obviously criminal act was in pursuit of some official presidential duty, then the current Supreme Court holds that the President gets absolute immunity. That is, in a word, absurd, and is made worse given that the Supreme Court has also effectively legalized bribery.
### 2\. Bribery Legalized
Perhaps the most obviously recognized form of corruption is bribery. It's why politicians have a bad rep, rightfully, for often favoring the wealthy and well connected while undermining fairness for everyone else. This week the Supreme Court ruled that maybe bribery isn't so bad after all? As Katya Schwenk of _Jacobin_ [summarizes](https://substack.com/redirect/66f7a1f7-c30a-474a-ba69-89aac1a40fdc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> The court's conservative supermajority ruled 6-3 in _Snyder v. United States_ , overturning the 2019 corruption conviction of an Indiana mayor who pocketed $13,000 from a local business tycoon after ensuring the company got a major town contract. The justices ruled that such bribes were not against the law.
This decision effectively makes bribery acceptable, undermining the integrity of our public officials and eroding public trust in government. In one way it removes the facade of the 2010 _Citizens United_ ruling that allowed for unlimited dark money and corporate money to enter political campaigns. Now, billionaires don't have to jump through the veneer of campaign donations to buy their favorite politicians--they can just bribe politicians directly. All thanks to our wonderful Supreme Court.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.._tUyjHdqTIiAlIZMSr4KWZiCDX93QnhP7RxcaNPtUoY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=146173786)
### 3\. Homelessness Criminalized
Not content with legalizing bribery, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in _Martin v. Boise_ that it is legal for cities to criminalize homelessness--because apparently sleeping is a crime. Understand how sinister and truly evil this ruling is. In 1865, the 13th Amendment codified prison slavery, leading to the passage of vagrancy laws to criminalize people on the street--forcing many formerly enslaved people back into prison slave labor. Now, in 2024, SCOTUS criminalizes homelessness, forcing people on the street into prison slave labor. Slavery is making a SCOTUS endorsed comeback, again.
And this is not hyperbole. Consider that [housing is 80% more expensive now](https://substack.com/redirect/68e60e82-ad69-4152-a0e4-f62710a4a8f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than just four years ago, and with [78% of Americans living paycheck to paycheck](https://substack.com/redirect/1b2069d4-303c-41ef-9959-0b02cf828c35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), this ruling effectively sanctions modern prison slave labor for the prison industrial complex by forcing homeless people into prison. This SCOTUS ruling is reminiscent of how, in 1933, Nazis passed a law "against Habitual & Dangerous Criminals," which relocated beggars, the homeless, and the unemployed to concentration camps.
Even worse, the Nazis built their laws off USA's Jim Crow laws. As Professor James Q. Whitman writes in his book, [Hitler's American Model](https://substack.com/redirect/9d62dcd2-e6cf-4c8d-995d-97def5bcd00d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> The Nuremberg Laws were crafted with considerable attention to the precedents American race laws had to offer. German praise for American practices, already found in Hitler's _Mein Kampf_ , was continuous throughout the early 1930s, and the most radical Nazi lawyers were eager advocates of the use of American models. Both American citizenship and anti-miscegenation laws proved directly relevant to the two principal Nuremberg Laws--the Citizenship Law and the Blood Law.
And to paraphrase Professor Whitman, the ultimate, ugly irony is that when Nazis rejected American practices, it was sometimes not because they found them too enlightened, _but too harsh_. And today the Supreme Court revives laws so harsh even genocidal Nazis thought they were too extreme.
### 4\. Insurrection Decriminalized
I'm old enough to remember when insurrection was considered a bad thing. No more, thanks to the Supreme Court. As Ian Millhauser writes for _[Vox](https://substack.com/redirect/18523790-0c52-4b71-b340-f58c5f8254fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ :
> On Friday, the Supreme Court ruled that a federal law, which states that anyone who "obstructs, influences, or impedes any official proceeding, or attempts to do so" commits a very serious federal crime, does not actually apply to everyone who obstructs, influences, or impedes an official proceeding. The Court made this ruling in a case involving a January 6 insurrectionist. Approximately 330 people who allegedly participated in that insurrection are charged with violating the statute at issue in Fischer v. United States, including Donald Trump. Friday's decision could potentially undermine much of the Justice Department's ability to prosecute hundreds of people who attacked the U.S. Capitol.
Where does this end? Can people walk into Congress right now and smear feces on the wall and claim it is not an obstruction? What about a state legislature? City Council? If feces is considered OK, what about vomit? Where does the Supreme Court draw the line to these absurdities? Who knows--but one thing is for sure--this ruling is another step towards fascism and rule of might, as opposed to rule of justice.

### 5\. Abortion Care Denied (To Kill More Women)
Two years ago the Supreme Court overturned a half century of precedent when they overturned Roe. The results have been devastating. Mothers in states with abortion bans are [three times more likely to die now](https://substack.com/redirect/ef6cabb9-291c-463f-aa00-cf677684153e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), than before Roe was overturned. Infant mortality has [spiked by nearly 13%](https://substack.com/redirect/62e5065a-e56b-46fb-af69-9f702fe31ff5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in states that ban abortion care.
The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 to dismiss a case on providing abortion care to women whose life is at risk, and did so while refusing to rule on the merits of the case. This sends the case back to lower courts to decide what to do--meanwhile women continue to die. As NPR [reports](https://substack.com/redirect/27d2f23b-353c-4171-934e-3ae2132cb403?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> Idaho is one of six states that have abortion bans that do not include exceptions for the health of the mother. The other states are South Dakota, Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas and Mississippi. The federal government has a law known as the Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act - or EMTALA - which says that anyone who comes into the emergency room must be stabilized before they're discharged or transferred. The Biden administration argued that should apply, even if the treatment is an abortion, and the patient is in a state that bans abortion with very limited exceptions. The court, in a 6-3 vote, dismissed the case, without ruling on its merits. The court did _not_ establish that EMTALA is the standard across the country.
So while for now, in Idaho ER doctors can provide abortion healthcare to women whose life is at risk, the other five states have no such obligation. Moreover, the fact that a woman needs to be literally on her death bed before doctors act is beyond dystopian, and speaks to why maternal mortality rates have tripled since Roe was overturned. The Supreme Court had a chance to undo the harm they've done, at least in part, but instead they've chosen a deliberate policy that demonstrably kills more women and babies.
### 6\. Corporate Pollution Unchecked
Finally, the Supreme Court decided that we do not actually need clean air, land, or water. In a significant shift, SCOTUS has ruled that federal environmental agencies no longer have the authority to define regulations unless explicitly outlined by Congress. As Amy Howe writes for [SCOTUSblog](https://substack.com/redirect/5433c5df-593d-4a21-a962-a1bd6069b016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> By a vote of 6-3, the justices overruled their landmark 1984 decision in _**[Chevron v. Natural Resources Defense Council](https://substack.com/redirect/7b3408df-e729-4c46-9302-5d36210cd6de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ , which gave rise to the doctrine known as the _Chevron_ doctrine. Under that doctrine, if Congress has not directly addressed the question at the center of a dispute, a court was required to uphold the agency's interpretation of the statute as long as it was reasonable. But in a 35-page ruling by Chief Justice John Roberts, the justices rejected that doctrine, calling it "fundamentally misguided."
This decision overturns a 1984 Chevron case ruling that empowered the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to regulate pollution. Now, corporations can pollute at will, with no governmental oversight. So much for the guidance of experts, combatting climate change, or ensuring corporations are regulated by government and not vice versa. As we experience existential climate change as the biggest threat modern humans have ever faced ([per the UN](https://substack.com/redirect/b9993c9a-e3d8-4caf-a2c8-b06972bcd350?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), you can thank the Supreme Court for ensuring it only gets worse from here.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.._tUyjHdqTIiAlIZMSr4KWZiCDX93QnhP7RxcaNPtUoY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=146173786)
### In Conclusion
As I have written before, it is critical we [expand the Court](https://substack.com/redirect/6b844d1f-b0cb-48cc-bc1f-2e9bb613edcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--but we cannot stop there. The Supreme Court's rulings this session represent a significant shift towards authoritarianism, undermining democratic principles, and increasing the power of corporations and the wealthy elite. The historical parallels to Jim Crow America and Nazi Germany are chilling, reminding us of the dangers of unchecked power and the importance of safeguarding our democratic institutions. The Court's decisions threatens the very foundation of our democracy.

The Supreme Court is here to tell you that you're wrong. Justice Sonia Sotomayor accurately lambasted the absurdity of this : "Today's decision to grant former Presidents criminal immunity reshapes the institution of the Presidency. It makes a mockery of the principle, foundational to our Constitution and system of Government, that no man is above the law. The majority today endorses an expansive vision of Presidential immunity that was never recognized by the Founders, any sitting President, the Executive Branch, or even President Trump's lawyers, until now. Settled understandings of the Constitution are of little use to the majority in this case, and so it ignores them. This ruling additionally delays significant legal cases past critical election dates, laying the groundwork for potential abuse of presidential power and further entrenching autocracy. As long as the President can make some excuse that his obviously criminal act was in pursuit of some official presidential duty, then the current Supreme Court holds that the President gets absolute immunity. That is, in a word, absurd, and is made worse given that the Supreme Court has also effectively legalized bribery. 2\. Bribery Legalized Perhaps the most obviously recognized form of corruption is bribery. It's why politicians have a bad rep, rightfully, for often favoring the wealthy and well connected while undermining fairness for everyone else. This week the Supreme Court ruled that maybe bribery isn't so bad after all? As Katya Schwenk of Jacobin : The court's conservative supermajority ruled 6-3 in Snyder v. United States , overturning the 2019 corruption conviction of an Indiana mayor who pocketed $13,000 from a local business tycoon after ensuring the company got a major town contract. The justices ruled that such bribes were not against the law. This decision effectively makes bribery acceptable, undermining the integrity of our public officials and eroding public trust in government. In one way it removes the facade of the 2010 Citizens United ruling that allowed for unlimited dark money and corporate money to enter political campaigns. Now, billionaires don't have to jump through the veneer of campaign donations to buy their favorite politicians--they can just bribe politicians directly. All thanks to our wonderful Supreme Court. 3\. Homelessness Criminalized Not content with legalizing bribery, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Martin v. Boise that it is legal for cities to criminalize homelessness--because apparently sleeping is a crime. Understand how sinister and truly evil this ruling is. In 1865, the 13th Amendment codified prison slavery, leading to the passage of vagrancy laws to criminalize people on the street--forcing many formerly enslaved people back into prison slave labor. Now, in 2024, SCOTUS criminalizes homelessness, forcing people on the street into prison slave labor. Slavery is making a SCOTUS endorsed comeback, again. And this is not hyperbole. Consider that than just four years ago, and with , this ruling effectively sanctions modern prison slave labor for the prison industrial complex by forcing homeless people into prison. This SCOTUS ruling is reminiscent of how, in 1933, Nazis passed a law "against Habitual & Dangerous Criminals," which relocated beggars, the homeless, and the unemployed to concentration camps. Even worse, the Nazis built their laws off USA's Jim Crow laws. As Professor James Q. Whitman writes in his book, : The Nuremberg Laws were crafted with considerable attention to the precedents American race laws had to offer. German praise for American practices, already found in Hitler's Mein Kampf , was continuous throughout the early 1930s, and the most radical Nazi lawyers were eager advocates of the use of American models. Both American citizenship and anti-miscegenation laws proved directly relevant to the two principal Nuremberg Laws--the Citizenship Law and the Blood Law. And to paraphrase Professor Whitman, the ultimate, ugly irony is that when Nazis rejected American practices, it was sometimes not because they found them too enlightened, but too harsh. And today the Supreme Court revives laws so harsh even genocidal Nazis thought they were too extreme. 4\. Insurrection Decriminalized I'm old enough to remember when insurrection was considered a bad thing. No more, thanks to the Supreme Court. As Ian Millhauser writes for : On Friday, the Supreme Court ruled that a federal law, which states that anyone who "obstructs, influences, or impedes any official proceeding, or attempts to do so" commits a very serious federal crime, does not actually apply to everyone who obstructs, influences, or impedes an official proceeding. The Court made this ruling in a case involving a January 6 insurrectionist. Approximately 330 people who allegedly participated in that insurrection are charged with violating the statute at issue in Fischer v. United States, including Donald Trump. Friday's decision could potentially undermine much of the Justice Department's ability to prosecute hundreds of people who attacked the U.S. Capitol. Where does this end? Can people walk into Congress right now and smear feces on the wall and claim it is not an obstruction? What about a state legislature? City Council? If feces is considered OK, what about vomit? Where does the Supreme Court draw the line to these absurdities? Who knows--but one thing is for sure--this ruling is another step towards fascism and rule of might, as opposed to rule of justice. 5\. Abortion Care Denied (To Kill More Women) Two years ago the Supreme Court overturned a half century of precedent when they overturned Roe. The results have been devastating. Mothers in states with abortion bans are , than before Roe was overturned. Infant mortality has in states that ban abortion care. The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 to dismiss a case on providing abortion care to women whose life is at risk, and did so while refusing to rule on the merits of the case. This sends the case back to lower courts to decide what to do--meanwhile women continue to die. As NPR : Idaho is one of six states that have abortion bans that do not include exceptions for the health of the mother. The other states are South Dakota, Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas and Mississippi. The federal government has a law known as the Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act - or EMTALA - which says that anyone who comes into the emergency room must be stabilized before they're discharged or transferred. The Biden administration argued that should apply, even if the treatment is an abortion, and the patient is in a state that bans abortion with very limited exceptions. The court, in a 6-3 vote, dismissed the case, without ruling on its merits. The court did not establish that EMTALA is the standard across the country. So while for now, in Idaho ER doctors can provide abortion healthcare to women whose life is at risk, the other five states have no such obligation. Our commitment is to push for pro-growth policies and make a stand against any actions that impede economic liberty. **This is how we 're getting it done:** **1. Advocacy at Every Level:** Our team works tirelessly to ensure that lawmakers hear the voice of fiscal conservatives loud and clear.

Peter,

Two days after AIPAC spent more money than has ever been spent in a U.S.
House primary, 62 Democrats joined Republicans in voting against counting
the amount of Palestinians killed by Israel in Gaza.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/signup/20240701-oppose-palestinian-casualties-censorship/?source=em20240701-35563&akid=35563%2E1203867%2Emk7Rau ]Tweet from Prem Thakker: Here are the 62 Democrats who joined 207

Health Ministry, undermining the organization’s death & injury figures.

Tell us again that AIPAC isn't a threat to our democracy.

This horrendous amendment would prevent the Department of State from using
any international affairs funding to cite death and injury statistics from
the Gaza Health Ministry.

It came the same week that Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump
used the word “Palestinian” as an attempted slur against President Biden
in their first debate.

Like our Justice Democrats incumbent Rep. Rashida Tlaib said, “There is so
much anti-Palestinian racism in this chamber that my colleagues don't even
want to acknowledge that Palestinians exist at all. Not when they're
alive—and now, not even when they're dead."

A vote for this amendment is a vote to deny genocide,
Peter. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/signup/20240701-oppose-palestinian-casualties-censorship/?source=em20240701-35563&akid=35563%2E1203867%2Emk7Rau ]Will you add your name to urge the
Senate to oppose this dangerous move that would censor facts and

has on Congress — and exactly why we need to re-elect our progressive
incumbents standing up for humanity.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

To clarify: No legislative districts have endorsed any candidates officially, to include Kim This includes: LD2, LD3, LD4, LD5 & LD8 While some members within the LDs are supportive of the campaign, this does represent the entire body.
